en.title: Christopher Nolan Film Boosts Assassin's Creed Odyssey Player Count by 90%
en.summary: A recent Christopher Nolan film has unexpectedly reignited interest in Ubisoft's ancient Greek RPG, Assassin's Creed Odyssey. Daily active users have surged, nearly doubling in the wake of the cinematic release.
en.body:
It appears that the magic of ancient Greece, as depicted on the silver screen, has successfully lured players back to Ubisoft's sprawling open-world adventure, **Assassin's Creed Odyssey**. Following the July 17th premiere of **Christopher Nolan**'s film, simply titled *Odyssey*, analyst data reveals a remarkable surge in daily active users (DAUs) across all major platforms. The game, originally released in 2018, saw its player base swell by an impressive 90%, jumping from 122,000 DAUs on the film's opening day to a staggering 233,000 within just ten days.

This near doubling of player engagement is particularly noteworthy given Ubisoft's minimal promotional efforts tying the game to the film. Reports indicate that the company's involvement was largely limited to a few social media posts subtly connecting the interactive experience to Nolan's cinematic vision. Despite this hands-off approach, the allure of exploring the vibrant world of ancient Greece, perhaps inspired by the film's narrative and visual spectacle, proved more than enough to draw players in. The growth was most pronounced on Xbox, where DAUs saw a dramatic 134% increase, climbing from 36,000 to 84,000. PlayStation users also showed significant renewed interest, with player numbers nearly doubling to 114,000, while Steam saw a respectable 26% rise.

## A Resurgence for Kassandra and Alexios

This unexpected resurgence highlights a fascinating trend in the gaming landscape: the enduring appeal of well-crafted, story-rich titles and the potent synergy between film and video games. For fans who may have missed **Assassin's Creed Odyssey** upon its initial release, or those who completed it years ago and are now feeling the pull of its Hellenic setting, this presents the perfect opportunity to dive back in. The game's rich historical setting, engaging combat, and compelling narrative featuring protagonists Kassandra and Alexios offer dozens of hours of exploration and discovery. The fact that this surge occurred with minimal marketing from Ubisoft speaks volumes about the game's inherent quality and the power of a well-timed cultural moment, proving that even years after its launch, **Assassin's Creed Odyssey** still has plenty to offer.

## What's Next for Odyssey and Beyond

While details on any further official cross-promotional activities between Ubisoft and **Christopher Nolan**'s *Odyssey* film have not yet been announced, the data clearly shows a sustained interest in the game. Players looking to experience this surge in activity can jump into **Assassin's Creed Odyssey** on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. It remains to be seen if this trend will influence future Ubisoft titles or their marketing strategies, but for now, it's a win for players and a testament to the lasting power of a beloved franchise.
